findings.issue_text: [High/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:290 small-action `a` in `.small-action`/`.top-topic` block: light-theme value silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 70% lightness via dark-light-choose; light themes now render the link at 70% instead of 30%, and the transformation should have kept 30% and only added the dark-theme branch.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:101 `.custom-message-length`: light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness, so light themes get 30% instead of 70%, and mobile no longer matches desktop/modal.scss:50 which uses 70%/30%.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:181 `h3` inside `a.star`: light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%, altering light-theme appearance and diverging from the equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss:320, still 20%).

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 `.user-content .name`: light-theme value changed from 30% to 50% instead of preserving 30% (should be 30%/70%), losing the visual distinction between `.name` and `.title` (both now 50%/50%).

[Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:239 `.badge-notification` background uses `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` in dark themes while its text color is `$secondary` (also dark in dark themes), producing very low text/background contrast in dark color schemes.

[Low/test_gap] No tests/screenshot/visual-diff coverage for a sweeping color change across ~40 rules; at minimum a dark-scheme visual regression check of admin, topic-list, and post streams should be run before merge.

The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:290 small-action `a` in `.small-action`/`.top-topic` block: light-theme value silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 70% lightness via dark-light-choose; light themes now render the link at 70% instead of 30%, and the transformation should have kept 30% and only added the dark-theme branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` near the shown hunk (`@@ -288,10 +288,10 @@`), the `.small-action` block’s `a` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This definitively changes the light-theme (first arg) value from 30% to 70% lightness, unlike the other substitutions in the diff which generally preserve the original `$primary` lightness and add a `$secondary` branch. So the finding is verifiably grounded and indicates an unintended light-theme regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:101 `.custom-message-length`: light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness, so light themes get 30% instead of 70%, and mobile no longer matches desktop/modal.scss:50 which uses 70%/30%.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` the `.custom-message-length` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Assuming `dark-light-choose(light, dark)` (as used elsewhere in this diff), this makes the light-theme value `30%` lightness instead of the prior `70%`. This also diverges from `desktop/modal.scss`, where `.custom-message-length` is updated to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e., the opposite pairing. The mismatch and apparent argument inversion are directly verifiable in the diff and plausibly cause incorrect light-theme styling on mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:181 `h3` inside `a.star`: light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%, altering light-theme appearance and diverging from the equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss:320, still 20%).

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss, the `a.star h3` color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which raises the light-theme lightness from 20% to 50%. In the same PR, the equivalent desktop rule (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` near the `a.star h3` block) keeps the light-theme value at 20% (now wrapped in `dark-light-choose(...20%..., ...80%...)`). This diff-grounded inconsistency plausibly introduces a mobile-only visual regression in light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:239 `.badge-notification` background uses `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` in dark themes while its text color is `$secondary` (also dark in dark themes), producing very low text/background contrast in dark color schemes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss`, `.badge-notification` was changed to `background-color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`, meaning the dark-theme background is derived from `$secondary`. The same rule sets link text via `&[href] { color: $secondary; }`, so in dark theme both foreground and background are based on `$secondary` (one scaled, one not), which can plausibly yield poor contrast/readability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] No tests/screenshot/visual-diff coverage for a sweeping color change across ~40 rules; at minimum a dark-scheme visual regression check of admin, topic-list, and post streams should be run before merge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes a sweeping, cross-cutting visual change: many SCSS rules replace `scale-color($primary, ...)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary,...), scale-color($secondary,...))` across admin, topic lists, header, posts, etc. No corresponding test/visual-regression artifacts are added in the diff, so it’s a reasonable review concern that this broad theming change should be validated (especially in dark scheme) even though it’s not a code correctness defect per se.
